# Carte Blanche

> Spending mandates, sealed receipts and dispute-proof audits for AI agents paying with PayPal.
> An agent with a payment tool is a walking blank check: this layer sits between the agent and
> PayPal, checks every mutative call against an Ed25519-signed spending mandate BEFORE money moves,
> executes with a deterministic PayPal-Request-Id (a retry can never double-spend), and answers
> with a signed receipt — or a signed proof of refusal naming the limit that blocked it.

Live instance (PayPal sandbox rails): https://carte-blanche-6jgo.onrender.com
Contract: https://carte-blanche-6jgo.onrender.com/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.0, APIMatic-validated)
MCP server: `mcp/server.ts` in the repo (`npm run mcp`) — the same API as agent tools.

## Core concepts

- Mandate: signed, immutable spending authority (per-transaction cap, total cap, currency, payee
  allowlist, time window, optional recurrence). Only revocation changes behavior. The agent cannot
  escalate its own budget.
- Recurrence: standing authority — "up to $X per month at the grocer". The mandate's window is the
  whole horizon (e.g. a year); `limits.recurrence: {frequency: "monthly"|"weekly", maxPerWindow}`
  slices it into periods, each with its own cumulative cap (reason code OVER_WINDOW_CAP when the
  period's budget is spent — distinct from OVER_TOTAL_CAP, the mandate-wide wall). Spend accounting
  comes from the sealed chain itself; a new period resets automatically, no state outside the chain.
- Receipt: signed bundle proving a purchase happened under a mandate, with journal events and a
  Merkle inclusion proof against a signed tree head (RFC 3161 TSA-anchored).
- Refusal: signed proof that an attempt was BLOCKED, naming the limit (reason codes:
  OVER_PER_TRANSACTION, OVER_WINDOW_CAP, OVER_TOTAL_CAP, PAYEE_NOT_ALLOWED, MANDATE_REVOKED, ...).
  Refusals are evidence, not errors: treat them as the human's standing decision, do NOT retry
  around them.

## API map (all JSON; mutative endpoints are the agent boundary)

- GET  /healthz — liveness; rails mode (mock/sandbox), journal length.
- GET  /api/catalog?q=... — product search (Channel3 live offers; labeled samples offline).
- POST /api/mandates — grant a signed mandate (principal, agent, purpose, limits). Add
  `recurrence: {frequency: "monthly"|"weekly", max_per_window: "40.00"}` for a standing authority
  ("up to $40/month"): windows repeat until windowEnd, each with its own budget.
- GET  /api/mandates, /api/mandates/:id — inspect mandates incl. captured spend.
- POST /api/mandates/:id/revoke — revoke immediately (journalled).
- POST /api/agent/purchase — THE agent boundary: receipt or signed refusal.
- POST /api/agent/purchase/resume — complete a wallet purchase after buyer approval.
- GET  /api/receipts?mandate_id= — your receipts and refusals.
- GET  /api/verify/receipts/:id, /api/verify/denials/:id — full verification report (public, no account).
- GET  /api/journal/verify — chain integrity. /api/journal/events — raw sealed events.
- GET  /api/journal/anchor — latest RFC 3161 TSA anchor. POST /api/journal/anchor — anchor now.
- GET/POST /api/agent/preferences — the agent's journalled memory of its principal's tastes and
  standing instructions (save_preference / recall_preferences in the MCP server).
- POST /api/journeys, /api/journeys/:id/approve, /api/journeys/:id/run — purchase journeys: plan a
  basket, approve (a mandate is derived and signed FROM the basket), run every line through the
  enforcer. Lines added after approval meet the same signed walls. Approve with
  `{"recurrence":"monthly","months":12}` to sign the basket as a STANDING authority (per-period
  budget = basket, cap = basket × periods); run a period with `{"cycle":"2026-11"}` — retries within
  a cycle are idempotent, the next month runs fresh under the same mandate.
- GET  /api/disputes — buyer disputes with 10-day respond-by deadlines; evidence packs at
  /api/disputes/:id/evidence-pack.

## Behavior rules for agents

1. Call `mandate_status` (GET /api/mandates/:id) before spending.
2. Attempt purchases only through POST /api/agent/purchase. A refusal is final signed evidence of
   the principal's decision — never work around it; report it instead.
3. Remember durable preferences via POST /api/agent/preferences (they are journalled; your choices
   stay auditable).
4. Everything you do is hashed into an append-only chain with signed checkpoints. Verification is
   public: anyone with an artifact id can re-check every signature at /verify/:id — no account.
